A.explanation: Work is $p\Delta V = 4000 \times 0.015 = 60 \text{ J}$ after converting to SI units.

B.explanation: This converts area to $0.05 \text{ m}^2$ but leaves distance as $30 \text{ cm}$, giving $4000 \times 0.05 \times 30 = 6000 \text{ J}$.

C.explanation: This converts distance to $0.30 \text{ m}$ but leaves area as $500 \text{ cm}^2$, giving $4000 \times 500 \times 0.30 = 6.0 \times 10^5 \text{ J}$.

D.explanation: This uses $500$ and $30$ directly in cm without conversion to metres, giving $4000 \times 500 \times 30 = 6.0 \times 10^7 \text{ J}$.

hints: Notice the area is $500 \text{ cm}^2$, the distance is $30 \text{ cm}$, but pressure is $4000 \text{ Pa}$ in SI units - both lengths must become metres.
Recall work against constant pressure can be found from force times distance with $F = pA$, or from $W = p\Delta V$ with $\Delta V = A \times d$.
Calculate $\Delta V$ in $\text{m}^3$ first, then multiply by $4000 \text{ Pa}$ and check the result is in joules and of order tens of joules.
walkthrough: Convert area and distance to SI units: $A = 500 \text{ cm}^2 = 500 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2 = 0.050 \text{ m}^2$ and $d = 30 \text{ cm} = 0.30 \text{ m}$.
Find the volume of gas displaced: $\Delta V = A \times d = 0.050 \times 0.30 = 0.015 \text{ m}^3$.
Use work done against constant pressure: $W = p\Delta V$.
Substitute values with units: $W = 4000 \text{ Pa} \times 0.015 \text{ m}^3 = 60 \text{ J}$.
Since $1 \text{ Pa} \times 1 \text{ m}^3 = 1 \text{ J}$, the unit check is correct. This is option A.
